name: Mahdi Tomb and Khalifa House
subtitle: Historic memorial complex and mudbrick residence marking the capital of the 19th-century Mahdist State.

facts.label: Khalifa House
facts.value: Constructed 1888 in traditional mudbrick and burnt brick

facts.label: Museum collection
facts.value: Mahdist weapons, banners, coinage, and colonial battle relics

parts.text: The political and spiritual heart of the historical Mahdist State in Omdurman. The silver-domed mausoleum honors Muhammad Ahmad al-Mahdi, whose forces captured Khartoum in 1885. The original structure was razed by Anglo-Egyptian troops in 1898 and rebuilt with its distinctive conical dome in 1947 by his son, Sayyid Abd al-Rahman al-Mahdi. Immediately adjacent stands the Khalifa House, a sprawling two-storey burnt-brick residence built in 1888 for Khalifa Abdallahi ibn Muhammad, preserved since 1928 as an ethnographic and historical museum.

gaps: Museum opening status and collection conditions during recent urban hostilities in Omdurman require field assessment.
